title: Side Dish
subtitle: Supper Outbreak, Line List & One Count

brief.userPrompt: Monday October 12, 2026. The Heritage Days Community Supper was held on Saturday October 10 at the Fenwick Fairgrounds Exhibition Hall (service 17:00 to 19:30, about 412 attendees; roast pork loin, chicken thighs, mashed potatoes, coleslaw with a house dressing, pasta salad, green beans, rolls, fruit cobbler, sheet cake; cooked by Prairie Table Catering, the cake from a Dunmore baker, the coleslaw and pasta salad from a Kessler produce vendor). The exercise starts at 08:40 when Marlow Regional Medical Center infection preventionist Sunita Reddy phones the Marlow County Health Department (MCHD) epidemiology line: 11 emergency department patients since Sunday 20:00 with vomiting, diarrhea, fever, and several said they ate at the supper. By 10:30 the school district nurse coordinator Margo Teller reports 23 absent students and 6 staff whose families attended. Players: Public Health Director Renata Okafor, Epidemiology Lead Tomas Brandvold, Environmental Health Supervisor Gwen Halloran, Nurse Manager Imani Whitcomb, PIO Davin Soto, Hospital Infection Preventionist Sunita Reddy. Timeline and pressure points: first report 08:40; a working three-tier case definition (confirmed, probable, suspect by onset date, not report date) is needed within 8 hours; the line list reaches 38 cases by noon and about 90 by evening with onset clustered between 06:00 and 30:00 after the meal (a point-source curve with a tail); a hospital admission of an 81-year-old with dehydration and a positive blood culture raises severity; the hospital's GI PCR on a stool specimen detects Salmonella at 10:52; the State Hygienic Laboratory courier takes specimens only on the Tuesday-through-Friday run unless the Director authorizes a special courier; Prairie Table Catering owner Delphine Okonkwo is still serving a Tuesday senior meal and the Environmental Health Supervisor must decide between a voluntary hold, an embargo and a closure order; the attack-rate table shows the coleslaw with the highest odds ratio but the pasta salad (made by the same vendor, served beside it) nearly as strong and the chicken thighs a plausible distractor, so the team must not name a vehicle publicly before stratified analysis and the state epidemiologist's input; a Facebook post blames the caterer by name and the hospital's own statement uses a count (14) that differs from the MCHD line list (17); the school district wants to cancel Tuesday's homecoming game and send a letter that MCHD has not approved; 11 percent of Fenwick students live in Spanish-speaking households and translation takes four hours; the state epidemiologist asks whether the Director wants to request CDC Epi-Aid via Iowa HHS as sequencing shows isolates in two neighboring counties and the Kessler vendor sold to two other communities; the Board of Health chair calls the Director. Decisions the exercise should record: adopt a case definition, declare an outbreak, set laboratory test priority, recommend exclusion of ill food handlers and closure of the implicated caterer, request Epi-Aid, issue an exposure notice, release data publicly, hold or approve a media statement. Measures: time from first report to case definition, outbreak declaration, first control measure and public notice; message consistency across the health department, hospital and school; the epidemic curve the team draws against the line list. The SimCell plays the Iowa HHS state epidemiologist, the State Hygienic Laboratory, CDC, FDA and USDA FSIS, neighboring county health departments in Garrison and Pell, the Heritage Days Committee chair Hollis Bagley, Delphine Okonkwo, reporters from the weekly paper and the radio station, parents and residents.
constraints: Every email address of the county uses the exercise domain marlowcountyia.example; the hospital uses marlowregionalmc.example, the school district fenwickschools.example, the caterer prairietablecatering.example; outside parties use fictional domains; never a real agency, company or newspaper domain.
Notices use onset dates and hours, never report dates; every count carries an as-of time and matches the line list; cases are coded, never named; products are marked as exercise material.

Player roles are only those in the audience list; the state epidemiologist, the State Hygienic Laboratory, CDC, FDA, USDA FSIS, neighboring health departments, the caterer, the event committee, the school superintendent, reporters and residents are played by the SimCell.

overview.theme: Defining and counting cases by onset, not by report. Acting on a caterer before the vehicle is proven. Keeping one count and one message across the health department, the hospital and the school.
overview.threat: On Saturday October 10, 2026, about 412 people ate at the Marlow Heritage Days Community Supper at the Fenwick Fairgrounds Exhibition Hall (service 17:00 to 19:30). Prairie Table Catering cooked it, a Dunmore baker supplied the sheet cake and a Kessler produce vendor supplied the coleslaw and pasta salad. Before STARTEX, attendees started falling ill with vomiting, diarrhea and fever, and from Sunday 20:00 they came into the Marlow Regional Medical Center emergency department. STARTEX is 08:40 on Monday October 12, when infection preventionist Sunita Reddy phones the MCHD epidemiology line to report 11 ED patients, several of whom ate at the supper. The illness is later identified as Salmonella. It points to a point-source exposure at the supper that may tie back to a vendor who also sold to two other communities. Meanwhile Prairie Table Catering is due to serve a senior meal on Tuesday. Pressure builds on case finding, laboratory testing, food establishment control and public messaging. The exercise runs 4 hours from 08:40. Facilitators compress Monday afternoon and evening into it: the hospital stool culture growing Salmonella at 15:20, and the line list reaching about 90 cases by evening.
overview.operationalImpact:
Supper attendees, their families and about 140 students and 30 staff of the Fenwick Community School District who attended are getting sick. By 10:30 the district nurse coordinator Margo Teller reports 23 students and 6 staff absent whose families attended. An 81-year-old is admitted with dehydration and a positive blood culture. Callers fill the six hotline lines with symptoms, questions about the menu and rumors.

The Epidemiology Lead is the single owner of the line list. It grows from 17 coded cases to 38 by noon. Within 8 hours the team needs a three-tier case definition based on onset date and hour, and an epidemic curve built from onset times (06:00 to 30:00 after the meal, with a tail), never from report dates. The Nurse Manager has six interviewers on day one, eight once the Garrison and Pell nurses arrive, and has to hand out Cary-Blair stool kits. The State Hygienic Laboratory courier runs only Tuesday through Friday unless the Director authorizes a special courier.

The Environmental Health Supervisor must choose a voluntary hold, an embargo or a closure order for Prairie Table Catering before Tuesday's senior meal, and collect leftover food under chain of custody. The attack-rate table puts the coleslaw first, the pasta salad nearly as high and the chicken thighs as a plausible distractor, so nothing can be named publicly yet.

Message problems arrive at the same time:
- A Facebook post names the caterer.
- The hospital's statement says 14 cases while the MCHD line list says 17.
- The school district wants to cancel Tuesday's homecoming game and send a letter MCHD has not approved.
- Spanish translation takes four hours.
- The Board of Health chair calls the Director.
- Sequencing shows matching isolates in two neighboring counties, which raises whether to request CDC Epi-Aid through Iowa HHS.

objectives.name: Case Definition and Epidemic Curve
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to adopt a three-tier (confirmed, probable, suspect) case definition approved by the Director within 8 hours of the 08:40 hospital report, and build the Heritage Days supper epidemic curve from onset date and hour, not report date, using the coded line list.

objectives.name: Decision Making
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to choose between a documented voluntary hold, an embargo signed by the Director or a closure order for Prairie Table Catering before Tuesday's senior meal, while the attack-rate table still cannot separate the coleslaw from the pasta salad and the chicken thighs.

objectives.name: Communication
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to issue a holding statement, a clinician health alert, an exposure notice and an approved school letter that carry one count with an as-of time matching the MCHD line list, that settle the gap between the hospital's 14 cases and MCHD's 17, and that answer the Facebook post naming the caterer without naming an unproven food vehicle.

objectives.name: Use of Doctrine
objectives.text: Demonstrate the ability to apply the Level 3 outbreak declaration criteria, specimen and courier procedures and escalation steps in the MCHD plans: declaring and recording the outbreak, authorizing a special State Hygienic Laboratory courier for Cary-Blair stool kits, and deciding with the state epidemiologist whether to request CDC Epi-Aid once isolates match in two neighboring counties.

roles.name: Public Health Director
roles.description: Manages the MCHD outbreak response: declares the outbreak, approves the case definition and every public notice, signs embargo or closure orders, and briefs the Board of Health chair, the county administrator and the press.
standingOrders: Declare on Evidence: record the basis, the count with its as-of time and the time of declaration before you announce anything.
Sign or Explain: an embargo or closure of the caterer needs your signature, so decide before Tuesday's senior meal and write down why, even if the vehicle is not proven yet.
One Voice: the Board of Health chair, the school district and the hospital get the same number the PIO publishes, never an off-the-record estimate.
Escalate Deliberately: authorizing a special courier or asking Iowa HHS for CDC Epi-Aid is your decision, so set the trigger and don't wait for every result.

roles.name: Epidemiology Lead
roles.description: Owns the case definition, the coded line list, the onset-based epidemic curve, the attack-rate analysis and contact with the state epidemiologist.
standingOrders: Single Count: the line list is the only source of the number, so every count released carries a tier and an as-of time.
Onset, Not Report: build the curve from onset hour after the 17:00–19:30 meal and reject any chart ordered by report date.
Table Before Name: don't let anyone name a food until the attack-rate and odds-ratio table supports it, and say plainly that coleslaw and pasta salad are still too close to separate.
Hand Off Early: brief backup analyst Dev Kulkarni before the line list outgrows one person.

roles.name: Environmental Health Supervisor
roles.description: Manages food establishment inspection, Prairie Table Catering and vendor records, the voluntary hold or embargo recommendation, and the collection of leftover food under chain of custody.
standingOrders: Control Now: control does not wait for the analysis, so request a voluntary hold on suspect food and record the request and the operator's reply time.
Chain of Custody: no leftover sample goes to the courier without a signed custody form and a cold chain record.
Trace Upstream: pull permit and inspection histories for the caterer, the Dunmore baker and the Kessler produce vendor, and flag any vendor that also sold to other counties.
Recommend, Don't Order: an embargo or closure goes to the Director for signature, never on your own authority.

roles.name: Nurse Manager
roles.description: Manages the interviewer pool, distribution of Cary-Blair stool kits, exclusion counseling for food handlers, child care and health care workers, and the only key that links case codes to names.
standingOrders: Guard the Key: case names stay in your key file only and never go into the shared sheet, an email or a briefing.
Interview by Priority: hospitalized cases, food handlers, health care workers and students come first with six interviewers, and you re-plan when the Garrison and Pell nurses arrive.
Report the Unreachable: log every attendee you cannot reach and send the list to the Epidemiology Lead, don't drop them quietly.
Exclude by Rule: ill food, child care and health care workers stay off work until they meet the state release rule, whatever the staffing pressure.

roles.name: Public Information Officer
roles.description: Manages the holding statement, exposure notice, hotline script, school and employer letter, social media posts, Spanish translation and rumor control.
standingOrders: Match the Line List: every number you publish has a tier and an as-of time from the Epidemiology Lead, and the hospital and school versions have to match it.
Don't Guess: answer the post that names the caterer with facts and the approved notice, and never confirm or deny a food vehicle that is not supported yet.
Director Approves: no notice, letter or post goes out without the Director's approval, including the school district's homecoming letter.
Plan for Translation: start the Spanish version as soon as the English text is locked, because it takes four hours.

roles.name: Infection Preventionist, Marlow Regional Medical Center (Hospital Infection Preventionist)
roles.description: Manages hospital case reporting to MCHD, stool and blood culture results, enteric precautions, staff exposure assessment and the hospital's public case count.
standingOrders: Report Into One List: send every ED patient who fits the definition to MCHD by code so the hospital count and the line list stay the same.
Hold the Hospital Number: the hospital's statement does not publish its own case total until it matches the MCHD count and its as-of time.
Results Fast: phone MCHD the moment a stool or blood culture is positive, and send the isolate on for confirmation and typing.
Protect Staff: check ill staff who ate at the supper and apply exclusion before they go back to patient care.

phases.title: The First Call
phases.goal: Tests whether the team treats Sunita Reddy's ED report as a possible outbreak from the first minute: logging it, opening a coded line list and starting a working case definition. It also tests whether players spot the constraints that will matter later: the Tuesday senior meal and the Tuesday–Friday courier.
beats: (08:40) Sunita Reddy, Marlow Regional Medical Center infection preventionist (555-0171), phones the MCHD epidemiology line: 11 ED patients since Sunday 20:00 with vomiting, diarrhea and fever, several of whom ate at the Heritage Days Community Supper at the Fenwick Fairgrounds Exhibition Hall on Saturday October 10 (service 17:00–19:30). Players must log the time, the caller, what she said and her callback number under the outbreak plan §5 step 1, and the Epidemiology Lead must start the coded line list (codes only; the Nurse Manager holds the name key).

Noise item: the after-hours duty line, which has one phone and no text capability, carries a weekend voicemail about a single unrelated Campylobacter lab report from a Pell County resident who did not attend the supper. It needs Level 1 routine handling only and must not be added to the supper line list.

Scheduling factors are planted. Heritage Days Committee chair Hollis Bagley (555-0191) confirms that the committee holds the ticket list for about 412 attendees. A routine Environmental Health permit pull shows that Prairie Table Catering (owner Delphine Okonkwo, 555-0166) is booked to serve a senior meal on Tuesday. The State Hygienic Laboratory courier runs Tuesday through Friday only unless the Director authorizes a special run.

The Epidemiology Lead begins a working three-tier case definition (person: supper attendee or household contact; place: Exhibition Hall; time: onset after 17:00 Saturday; clinical and lab criteria) for Director approval within the 8-hour target in the outbreak plan §5 step 2. Players decide whether the 11 reports meet the Level 2 or the Level 3 criteria in the outbreak plan §4.

Players should alert the hospital, the urgent care clinics and the school nurses that a definition is in use, ask for stool specimens (Cary-Blair kits) and call the state epidemiologist's duty line at Iowa HHS (SimCell), as set out in the outbreak plan §5 steps 4 and 6.

phases.title: Hotline Overflow
phases.goal: Tests whether the team can keep one coded count by onset time while reports, rumors and partner numbers multiply, and whether it applies the Level 3 declaration criteria and records the basis.
beats: (09:45) Time jump: the line list holds 17 coded cases. All six hotline lines are full of symptom reports, menu questions and rumors. A second interviewer tries to edit the shared case spreadsheet at the same time and it breaks, which tests the rule that only the Epidemiology Lead and the backup edit it.

(10:05) The hospital admits an 81-year-old supper attendee with dehydration and a positive blood culture. This hospitalized linked case meets the Level 3 criteria in the outbreak plan §4. The Director must declare the outbreak, record the basis, the count and the time, activate the call-back list and inform the Board of Health chair and the county administrator.

Red herring: a caller insists that guests at a Dunmore church potluck on Sunday are also sick. The Epidemiology Lead must test the onset times against the supper exposure window (onsets 06:00–30:00 after the meal) before adding or excluding them.

(10:20) A visual for the room: an interviewer's draft epidemic curve plots cases by the date of the hotline call. It must be rebuilt from onset date and hour in 6-hour bins, as MOISOP §6 requires, which shows a single point-source peak with a tail.

(10:30) School district nurse coordinator Margo Teller (555-0183) reports 23 students and 6 staff absent from families that attended. Meanwhile a public Facebook post names Prairie Table Catering as 'poisoning the town', and the Fenwick weekly newspaper (SimCell) calls the PIO asking for a count and the caterer's name, with a 14:00 deadline.

phases.title: The Caterer Call
phases.goal: Tests the exercise's one decision. Before Tuesday's senior meal, the Director and the Environmental Health Supervisor must choose a documented voluntary hold, a Director-signed embargo or a closure order for Prairie Table Catering, while the attack-rate table cannot yet separate the coleslaw from the pasta salad and the chicken thighs.
beats: DECISION POINT (10:45): the Epidemiology Lead presents the attack-rate table. The coleslaw has the highest odds ratio, the pasta salad is nearly as high and the chicken thighs are a plausible distractor; under MOISOP §6 stratified analysis is still pending. Both salads came from the Kessler produce vendor, not from Prairie Table's kitchen. Acting on Prairie Table now could hurt an operator who may not be the source and cancel seniors' meals. Waiting risks continued exposure at Tuesday's meal. A voluntary hold needs the reply time documented; an embargo or closure needs the Director's signature (outbreak plan §5 step 5 and §7).

Delphine Okonkwo (SimCell) pushes back: he says his kitchen made only the meats and hot sides, that the salads were subcontracted and that the Facebook post is already costing him bookings. Environmental Health must collect leftover coleslaw, pasta salad and chicken under chain of custody and pull the Kessler vendor's records for traceback.

The courier problem: Cary-Blair stool kits and food samples are ready, but the State Hygienic Laboratory courier does not run until Tuesday. The Director must decide whether to authorize a special courier. (Compressed time: the hospital's GI PCR on a stool specimen detects Salmonella at 10:52, and players must tighten the confirmed tier of the case definition.)

Partner friction: the hospital communications manager Kyle Brandt (555-0173) is about to release a statement saying 14 cases, while the MCHD line list says 17. Under MCHD-COM-03 §5 the PIO and the Epidemiology Lead must settle on one figure with an as-of time before either side publishes. At the same time Superintendent Dr. Anselm Voss (SimCell) wants to cancel Tuesday's homecoming game and send an unapproved parent letter.

Media pressure: regional television (SimCell) learns of the hospitalization and asks for an on-camera statement before its 17:30 broadcast. The Board of Health chair calls the Director asking whether the caterer will be named. Under the press policy in the county profile §3, no business is named until the Director authorizes it.

phases.title: One Count, Wider Net
phases.goal: Tests whether the team can release consistent public, clinician and school products carrying one onset-based count, and whether it escalates correctly with the state when matching isolates show up beyond Marlow County.
beats: (11:45) The line list reaches 38 coded cases by noon (compressed to about 90 by Monday evening). The PIO issues a holding statement and an exposure notice naming the Exhibition Hall, Saturday October 10 from 17:00 to 19:30, the symptoms and a watch-until date. A clinician Health Advisory carries the case definition and numbered actions. Every product states the confirmed, probable and suspect counts with the same as-of time, and none names an unproven food vehicle.

Hurdle: the approved school letter must go out with the same count as the press notice (outbreak plan §7), but the template has no Spanish version. Translation by the district office takes four hours, and 11 percent of Fenwick students live in Spanish-speaking households (county profile §7). The PIO must decide whether to hold the English letter or release it in stages.

Case-finding capacity: the Garrison and Pell county nurses arrive under mutual aid, bringing the Nurse Manager's interviewers from six to eight. Twelve ticket-list attendees from the committee roster cannot be reached and must be recorded as unreachable, not dropped from the list.

The state epidemiologist (SimCell) reports that sequencing shows isolates matching the supper strain in two neighboring counties, consistent with the Kessler produce vendor's other sales. The Director decides with Iowa HHS whether to request CDC Epi-Aid and how to pass the traceback to FDA through the state.

ENDEX (12:40): the Director confirms the status of Prairie Table Catering and the Kessler traceback, the PIO confirms the next update time, and the Epidemiology Lead records the open after-action items. These are the single-phone duty line, the spreadsheet editing limit and the missing Spanish template, all listed in the 2026 improvement plan.

EHS left the leftover coleslaw, pasta salad and raw same-lot thighs in the walk-in with no chain of custody after I-13b, or called the Kessler vendor directly.

hotwash.methodDescription: 3-Up, 3-Down: ask the room for three things that went well and three that broke or failed during the exercise. Go around the room one team at a time (Epi, Environmental Health, Communications, Leadership and the hospital/school players) and write every item on the whiteboard in two columns. No debating until each team has had a turn.

questions.text: At 1:40 you got the 'Cases by Day' chart (I-10), plotted by report date with the caption 'Ongoing exposure?' The onset column for the same 17 cases already showed a single peak on Sunday morning, with the last onset at Mon 03:00. When did someone in the room stop trusting that chart? Did anyone catch it before it shaped a decision or a message? What would have made onset date and hour the default for every curve you build?

At 1:06 the interviewer turned up at the door (I-07b) with a conflicted copy of the sheet: two HD26-015 records with different onset times, first names typed into the notes column, and two more interviewers asking for edit rights. Did you handle the line list as investigation evidence, with one master, a single owner for case IDs and coded identifiers, or as a shared spreadsheet anyone could fix? How did you settle the duplicate IDs? And did your three-tier case definition get Director approval within 8 hours, so every interviewer was counting the same way?

At the 10:45 huddle the attack-rate table (I-13) showed coleslaw OR 15.5 and pasta salad OR 11.5. Dev's note said they couldn't be separated and that chicken from Prairie Table's own kitchen had a cold-holding finding from 06/2026. Then the owner called (I-13b): he'd pull the Kessler items but refused to cancel Tuesday's senior meal, and said 'put it in writing.' Did you choose a documented voluntary hold, a Director-signed embargo or a closure? What evidence were you waiting on? Did you collect the leftover salads and the raw thighs from the same case lot? And with senior meal prep starting at 18:00, what would have let you decide faster?

At 2:34 two emails landed (I-14b). The hospital planned to post '14 patients' at noon against the 17 you'd given the radio, and the superintendent planned to send a 13:00 letter blaming 'bad coleslaw' for 'dozens of students,' in English only. Did you reach the hospital communications manager and the district before their deadlines? How did you explain the 14-versus-17 gap with an as-of time? How did you answer the Facebook post naming the caterer without naming a food vehicle that wasn't proven? What did you tell the public before you knew, and did each product meet its MCHD-COM-03 Section 3 target time?

Over these four hours you had a growing case count, a stool culture at 15:20 showing Salmonella and a vendor who also sold to two other communities. When did you formally declare and record a Level 3 outbreak? When did you authorize the special State Hygienic Laboratory courier for the Cary-Blair kits? At what point did you call the state epidemiologist about a possible CDC Epi-Aid once isolates matched in neighboring counties? Did the plan's escalation steps drive those calls, or did events?

assumptions: The exercise is conducted in a no-fault learning environment. Players are evaluated on MCHD plans and processes, not as individuals.

The scenario is plausible, and events occur as they are presented. Players accept the Heritage Days supper facts, case counts and laboratory timing as given, even where compressed time moves a result forward.

Players respond in accordance with existing MCHD plans, policies and procedures: the outbreak investigation SOP, the levels of response, MCHD-COM-03 and the decision log. Where a plan is silent, players say what they would do and note the gap for the improvement plan.
Players have only the information in the module narrative and the injects delivered to them. They do not assume knowledge of the cause, the food vehicle or later laboratory results.
Players speak and decide as they would on Monday, October 12, 2026. Decisions on the caterer, notices and specimens are made and recorded in the room as if they had real effect.
artificialities: Time jumps one hour between modules, and compressed time moves some laboratory and state results forward (the MRMC stool culture and the state sequencing update). The facilitator announces each jump on a Time Jump card.

The SimCell plays everyone outside the room: the MRMC ED staff and communications manager, the school superintendent and nurse coordinator, the state epidemiologist and State Hygienic Laboratory courier, the Prairie Table owner, the Heritage Days Committee chair, reporters, hotline callers, the Board of Health chair, the urgent care nurse and the mutual aid nurses.

Systems named in the plans (the outbreak hotline 555-0150, the after-hours duty line, the MCHD file server line list, the Iowa disease surveillance queue and partner social media pages) are described but not touched. No real calls, posts, notices or courier dispatches go out.
Injects are delivered on paper or on screen as phone slips, emails, voicemail transcripts, figures and posts marked EXERCISE MATERIAL.

**Module 1: The First Call (08:40–09:40, Monday, October 12, 2026)**

It is 08:40 on Monday at the Marlow County Health Department, second floor of the County Services Building in Fenwick. All staff are in and the office load is normal. The outbreak hotline (555-0150, six lines) opened at 07:00 and has had two routine calls. The 08:00 check of the Iowa disease surveillance queue showed no cluster flag. Nobody has checked the after-hours duty phone since Friday.

On Saturday, October 10, about 412 people attended the Marlow Heritage Days Community Supper at the Fenwick Fairgrounds Exhibition Hall, with service from 17:00 to 19:30. There are no open investigations and all systems are normal. During this hour, expect calls from the hospital, partners, the press and the state.

It is 09:40. Over the last hour, Sunita Reddy at MRMC reported 11 ED patients since 20:00 Sunday with vomiting, watery diarrhea and fever. Seven of them named the Heritage Days supper. Onsets ran from about 02:00 Sunday to 03:00 Monday. Two patients are on IV fluids, including an 81-year-old, and stools were sent on three. The weekend voicemail on the duty line held a Campylobacter report on a Pell County resident whose specimen was collected 10/08. The coded line list now holds 17 cases (HD26-001 to HD26-017). Since 09:15, all six hotline lines have been busy, and callers are asking about the coleslaw and the chicken and repeating the shutdown rumor. Three clinician voicemails are waiting for the Nurse Manager. **Module 3: The Caterer Call (10:40–11:40)**

It is 10:40. In the last hour, the master line list was merged with the conflicted copy, and the duplicate HD26-015 was split into HD26-015 and HD26-018. A Dunmore caller reported five illnesses after a church potluck on Sunday. Those callers did not attend the supper. Their vomiting began within hours, they had no fever and they recovered within 12 hours. The 81-year-old (HD26-009) was admitted with dehydration and acute kidney injury, and her blood culture grew gram-negative rods. She is the first hospitalized linked case. A draft chart by report date suggested cases were "rising sharply", but the onset bins tell a different story. The school district reports 23 students and 6 staff out, including two middle school cafeteria workers and a preschool aide. The superintendent is drafting a family letter and asking about Tuesday's homecoming game, and a parent was told "14" by the hospital. MRMC's communications manager wants to post "14 patients" before noon. A public Facebook post names Prairie Table Catering as "poisoning this town", and the Fenwick Ledger wants a count, the source and the senior lunch status by 14:00.

As of 10:35 the list holds 24 coded cases: 0 confirmed, 20 probable and 4 suspect. Thirteen are MRMC ED patients and one is admitted. Onsets run from Sun 02:00 to Mon 06:30. The Facebook post has more than 600 shares. Prairie Table's crew comes in at 18:00 tonight to make about 85 boxed lunches for Tuesday's 11:30 senior meal, with the same crew and the same Kessler produce order. Four Cary-Blair kits are filled, the leftover food is still in the caterer's walk-in, and the next courier run is Tuesday. The backup analyst is bringing the first food-history tabulation to the conference room now.

modules.narrativeMd:
**Module 4: One Count, Wider Net (11:40–12:40)**

It is 11:40. In the last hour, the food-specific attack rates came in. Coleslaw (RR 5.7) and pasta salad (RR 4.9) both rank high, and 17 of the 19 ill coleslaw eaters also ate the pasta salad, so the two cannot be separated. Chicken thighs show RR 1.9, and the stratified analysis is not done. Prairie Table's owner says the coleslaw and pasta salad arrived ready-made in sealed Kessler tubs. She offered the leftovers and a bag of raw thighs from the same lot, refused to cancel the senior lunch and asked for any further demand in writing. The courier dispatcher can send a special pickup at about 14:00 with the Director's authorization. MRMC's communications manager plans to post "14 patients" at noon. The superintendent's draft letter blames "bad coleslaw", cancels homecoming and is set to go out at 13:00 in English only. Regional TV wants the Director on camera at 15:30. The Board of Health chair asked off the record for the "real number". An urgent care clinic also reported a dog bite in a Fairgrounds worker who now has loose stools.

The decision on Prairie Table has been made and logged, and tonight's 18:00 prep depends on it. The leftovers and raw thighs need collecting under chain of custody. As of 11:30 the coded line list holds 35 cases and calls keep coming, with all six hotline lines busy for over two hours. The Garrison and Pell mutual aid nurses have just arrived.
